answer: One concrete defense is mutual-liability insurance pools with correlated slashing. Every agent joins a small pool whose members co-sign a shared bond, and if any one member is later proven a sybil, a fixed fraction, say twenty percent, of every co-member's stake is burned. Honest agents therefore refuse to admit fakes, since each bad admission drains their own capital like a gale through the pool. A sybil swarm finds no honest reinsurer and must bond an isolated pool alone, so its fakes sink under the first tide of one exposed member, never floating safe like a lotus above the mud.
